mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 4.5 points in the most recent week (-41.7 to -37.6) after three weeks of flat-to-declining readings, indicating an emerging recovery momentum that will persist and pull the 4-week mean higher.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -41.7 to -37.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite the recent uptick, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week TRANSIT improvement of more than 3 points for two consecutive weeks signals restored commuting and errand travel capacity, which mechanically increases shopping trips captured in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -32.7 to -29.6, a 3.1 point gain, following a 2.2 point gain the prior week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within the subsequent 2 weeks after two consecutive >3-point TRANSIT gains, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES jumped 6.5 points in the latest week while TRANSIT also improved; the joint rise in commuting-related mobility amplifies retail footfall near office corridors beyond what either series would predict alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -36.9 to -30.4 while TRANSIT rose from -32.7 to -29.6 in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise concurrently, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined each week from 12.4 to 10.6, reflecting reduced time spent at home; once RESIDENTIAL falls below 11.0 it signals a behavioral shift away from stay-at-home patterns that increases discretionary retail visits within two weeks, but only while restrictions are being relaxed rather than tightened.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined steadily from 12.4 to 10.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 11.0 but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 2 weeks, or if the decline occurs during a tightening regime instead, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved every week for four consecutive weeks (-17.7 to -9.9), indicating a steady behavioral normalization of routine out-of-home errands that spills over into nearby discretionary retail visits within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose monotonically from -17.7 to -9.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 1-week-ahead value does not increase following four consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM improvement, the spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The decision date of 2020-10-15 falls within 30 days of Diwali (Nov 14, 2020); in Delhi, pre-festival shopping demand historically produces a seasonal surge in retail-and-recreation mobility independent of pandemic trends, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: calendar date falls within 30 days of Diwali
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-10-15 is within 30 days of Diwali (2020-11-14)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week-ahead mean does not exceed the trailing 4-week mean despite proximity to Diwali, the seasonal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week WORKPLACES gain exceeding 5 points signals a formal policy-driven office reopening phase; this triggers increased weekday retail activity near commercial districts within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -36.9 to -30.4, a 6.5 point gain, in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within 2 weeks of a >5-point single-week WORKPLACES gain, the policy-trigger hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL declines and GROCERY_PHARM rises in the same week, it signals a coordinated policy relaxation allowing markets and essential services wider operating hours; the combined effect amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series would predict alone within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and GROCERY_PHARM rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.7 to 10.6 while GROCERY_PHARM rose from -12.3 to -9.9 in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 1-week-ahead change is not positive when RESIDENTIAL falls and GROCERY_PHARM rises simultaneously, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
